commitResults.messageTitle: Updated .gitignore, AGENTS.md, and changed the bot name to MoistBot
Updated MoistBot to greet and exit. Updated README to reflect changes
Add user input echo and exit functionality with SEEDU documentation
commitResults.messageBody:
- Implement Scanner-based input loop that echoes user messages
- Add exit condition when user types bye
- Add comprehensive Javadoc for class and main method
- Update documentation files with SEEDU standards (Git and Java coding conventions)

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor MoistBot to support task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody:
- Extract banner and divider as static constants to reduce duplication
- Move user input handling into a new parseInput() method
- Integrate task list functionality with list command support
- Allow tasks to be added by any non-bye input
- Update class documentation to reflect task management capability

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Task class and mark/unmark functionality
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce Task class to represent individual tasks with completion
status, replacing the string-based storage model. This enables
users to mark tasks as completed or incomplete via new mark and
unmark commands.

Changes:
- Create Task class with name and completion status
- Refactor List to store Task objects instead of strings
- Rename List methods: addText() → addTask(), printText() → printTasks()
- Add List.getTask(int id) to retrieve tasks by index
- Implement mark and unmark commands in parseInput()
- Improve command parsing to handle input arguments
- Update Javadoc comments to reflect new design

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename task manager class Rename the in-memory task list helper from List to TaskManager and update the references in MoistBot to match. This keeps the class name clearer and makes the task management role more explicit.

Refactor input handling into Command and Parser classes Extract input parsing and command handling logic from MoistBot into two new classes: Parser handles normalization and validation, Command encapsulates parsed command data. Update MoistBot to use these classes for clearer separation of concerns and easier maintenance.

Refactor UI and error handling into dedicated components Introduce UserInterface class to centralize all output formatting, separating presentation logic from command execution. Migrate error handling from Parser's error commands to exception-based approach, allowing MoistBot to catch and display errors via UI layer. Update Task and TaskManager to provide data accessors instead of printing directly, completing the inversion of control pattern where UI layer owns all output responsibility.

Refactor command parsing to use enum-based types and structured fields - Replace generic String-based command representation with CommandType enum - Add specialized fields (description, from, to) to Command class for different command needs - Implement dedicated parsers for deadline and event commands with validation - Add task type constants (TODO, DEADLINE, EVENT) to Task class - Update all command consumers to work with new enum-based architecture - Enhance error messages for missing or malformed arguments
commitResults.messageBody: This improves type safety and makes command handling more maintainable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor command handling and task creation Extract command-specific parsing and execution helpers to make the command flow easier to read and maintain.
commitResults.messageBody:
Centralise task creation and storage, make immutable task data final,
and update mark/unmark feedback and UI regression cases to reflect the
revised behaviour.

Extract command parsing and error handling into processCommand() to
simplify the main loop. Rename the exit flag for clearer boolean naming
and use the simplified task-list UI method.

Cover malformed task additions and invalid mark or unmark commands.
Verify that rejected commands preserve task list and completion state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add custom exception for chatbot errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Use MoistBotException for invalid commands, task operations, and
task-list capacity failures so chatbot-specific errors are handled
consistently.

Require agents to update relevant UI test cases and invoke the
test-ui skill after every code update.

Give users specific guidance for malformed commands, invalid task
numbers, missing task fields, and task-list capacity failures.

Reject unexpected arguments and malformed separators so invalid input
does not silently proceed. Add a fallback for unexpected runtime errors
to keep the application responsive.

Expand UI regression coverage for each error path and the 100-task
limit.

Explain that the task list is empty and show the available commands
when the user runs list without any tasks.

Update greetings, confirmations, validation errors, and unexpected-error
messages to use a clear, professional butler voice. Refresh UI regression
cases and documentation to reflect the revised console output.

Also make stateless utility classes non-instantiable and improve selected
Javadoc and naming details.

Group MoistBot classes by responsibility to make the project structure
clearer and prepare it for future growth.

Update the UI test runner to compile sources recursively and launch the
new fully qualified main class.

Correct the MoistBot source path after reorganizing the Java classes into
packages. Update the example console output to match the current greeting
and farewell messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task deletion and dynamic task storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the fixed-size task array with an ArrayList so the task list can
grow beyond 100 entries without an artificial capacity limit.

Add the delete command with validation and courteous feedback so users
can remove tasks safely. Update UI regression coverage for deletion,
invalid task numbers, renumbering, and dynamic resizing.

Write the complete task list to data/moistbot.txt after successful add,
mark, and unmark operations so changes persist between sessions.

Handle file-writing errors courteously and add regression coverage that
verifies the saved task format.

Read todos, deadlines, events, and their completion states from the task
data file when MoistBot starts.

Handle missing, unreadable, and malformed data safely. Add regression
coverage for successful loading and invalid saved data.

Use relative, platform-independent paths and handle missing or invalid
save files safely.

Write task data atomically, escape reserved characters, reject malformed
or oversized data, and roll back changes when saving fails. Expand UI
regression coverage for persistence edge cases.

Reject malformed records and blank lines before updating the task list so
corrupted files cannot cause partial loading.

Accept UTF-8 byte-order marks and expand regression coverage for invalid
types, flags, fields, encodings, and mixed valid and corrupted records.

Task-number validation belongs with the task collection rather than the
application entry point. Move the existing lookup and validation logic
into TaskManager so MoistBot can focus on coordinating commands, storage,
and UI feedback.

This preserves the current messages and behavior while giving task-list
operations a clearer home for the later instance-based refactor.

The task collection was held in static state, so storage, UI, and command
handling all depended on one hidden global list. Give each MoistBot object
its own TaskManager and make task operations instance methods instead.

Pass the owned task manager explicitly when saving or displaying tasks, and
have storage return loaded tasks to the application. This clarifies state
ownership and prepares the remaining collaborators for instance-based
composition without changing user-visible behavior.

Storage previously depended on one static file location, preventing a
MoistBot instance from defining where its tasks belong. Give Storage an
instance-owned path and let MoistBot construct and retain that service.

This makes persistence configuration explicit, supports isolated storage
locations, and moves the application composition closer to the intended OOP
design while preserving the existing production path and behavior.

MoistBot still created and controlled the console scanner even though user
interaction belongs to the UI abstraction. Give UserInterface ownership of
the scanner and convert its output operations to instance methods.

MoistBot now owns one UI object alongside its storage and task manager. This
keeps the main class focused on application flow and completes the target
separation without changing the console transcript.

Command execution still resides in MoistBot's central switch. Introduce the
common execution and exit-status protocol on Command, then move farewell and
termination behavior into a dedicated ExitCommand.

Parser now creates the specialized command for valid bye input. This provides
a small, behavior-preserving foundation for moving the remaining commands to
polymorphic execution one at a time.

List display remains in MoistBot even though the parser can select a command
object that owns this behavior. Add ListCommand and let it display the supplied
task collection through the UI.

Route list and bye through the same polymorphic execution path. This removes
another branch-specific method from MoistBot without introducing persistence
risk or changing the displayed task list.

Task additions share a persistence contract: add the task, save the updated
list, roll back if saving fails, and only then confirm success. Move this
workflow into an abstract AddCommand to keep concrete additions focused on
creating their task type.

Add TodoCommand as the first subtype and have Parser construct it. This moves
todo execution out of MoistBot and provides reusable behavior for deadline
and event extraction in subsequent increments.

Deadline execution still depends on a dedicated method in MoistBot even
though AddCommand now owns the common persistence workflow. Add a concrete
DeadlineCommand that creates the task from its parsed description and time.

Have Parser return the specialized command and route it through polymorphic
execution. This removes deadline-specific behavior from MoistBot while
preserving validation, rollback, and user feedback.

Represent event additions with a dedicated EventCommand so that event
creation uses the same polymorphic workflow as todo and deadline
commands.

This completes the AddCommand family and removes the final add-task
branch and helper methods from MoistBot. Keeping task creation inside
each command reduces the main class's responsibilities while preserving
the existing save, rollback, and user-feedback behavior.

Add dedicated commands for marking, unmarking, and deleting tasks, with
shared completion-state persistence and rollback behavior.

Make Command an abstract execution contract and let concrete commands
own their arguments. MoistBot can now execute every parsed command
polymorphically without a command-type switch or operation-specific
helpers, completing the command-pattern refactor.

Store deadline dates and optional times as java.time values so the
task model can reason about them instead of retaining raw text.

Accept ISO and day-first inputs, reject invalid values, display
friendly dates, and preserve canonical values across save and load
operations.

Store event endpoints as typed dates and optional times so events can
be interpreted consistently instead of retaining raw text.

Validate endpoint formats and ordering, display friendly ranges, and
preserve canonical values across save and load operations.

Allow list to accept an inclusive cutoff date and show only deadlines
due and events starting on or before that date.

Retain original task numbers, explain the active cutoff in the output,
and guide users when no dated tasks match.
Add date-aware deadlines, events, and filtering

Allow users to find tasks whose descriptions contain a given search
term. Provide clear feedback for missing terms and searches without
matches.

Add UI regression cases for successful and invalid searches.
Add task description search command

Clarify the responsibilities and contracts of the application entry point.

Document private workflows and their error handling for maintainers.
Improve MoistBot Javadoc comments

Replace placeholder and template documentation with a GitHub Pages-ready
guide covering setup, command syntax, task notation, date handling, and
persistence.

Keeping the root and docs copies aligned makes the guide available from both
the repository landing page and published documentation.
